solution: Work on the torus with 0-indexed coordinates and define the canonical point f(picture) = (Sr * w^{-1} mod n, Sc * w^{-1} mod n), where Sr and Sc are the sums of the rows and columns of the black cells and w is their count; w is invertible mod n exactly because gcd(n, w) = 1. This point is equivariant under the whole transformation group: a cyclic shift by (dr, dc) moves Sr by w*dr so f moves by (dr, dc); the 90-degree rotation sends f to (C, -1-R) and the reflection sends f to (R, -1-C), matching how a real cell moves; and inverting colors replaces (Sr, Sc, w) by (-Sr, -Sc, -w) mod n, leaving f unchanged. So Chtholly only has to make f equal the target x: she needs the black-cell sum to become (a*w mod n, b*w mod n), i.e. she must move one black cell by the fixed offset v = (a*w - Sr, b*w - Sc) mod n, which she does by swapping a black cell p with the white cell p+v; if no such p existed the black set would be invariant under translation by v, so the order k > 1 of v would divide both n and w, contradicting gcd(n, w) = 1 (and v = 0 means she swaps a cell with itself). Willem simply recomputes f on the picture he sees and prints it, which is the transformed target. Both runs cost O(n^2) time and O(n^2) memory. Verified on the first sample test (it reproduces the official swap 1 1 4 1) and by 3000 randomized simulations over every combination of shifts, rotations, reflections and inversions.

notes: The vocabulary has no label for a group-equivariant invariant (a canonical point that commutes with a symmetry group acting on the input) — that is the real idea here, and 'constructive-algorithm' plus 'modular-arithmetic' are the closest existing labels. There is also no 'communication' or 'run-twice' label; I used 'interactive' at lower confidence because this is jury-mediated two-program communication rather than a query loop, and the judge tags list both 'communication' and 'interactive'. The judge tag 'expression parsing' is a scrape artifact and has nothing to do with the problem.
